proposed_comments.title: Resolve each app-icon candidate end-to-end before advancing to the next fallback

confidence.rationale: The converged fork diff had to separately fix indexed candidates, missing rooted files, directly renderable SVG/image candidates, and duplicate extraction for ordinary executable candidates before the ordered-fallback loop became coherent.

proposed_comments.body:
### Resolve each app-icon candidate end-to-end before advancing to the next fallback

**Severity:** `high`

The current app-icon path still mixes thumbnail extraction and ordinary conversion in ways that let one candidate interfere with the next one. Indexed binary references, missing rooted files, directly renderable SVG/image candidates, and ordinary executable candidates need different handling, but the overall rule is the same: finish the current candidate's applicable resolution path before moving on. Otherwise an earlier valid candidate can be skipped, a missing candidate can surface an unrelated shell icon, or a cold executable path can pay duplicate extraction cost before the ordered fallback is even considered.

Please restructure the candidate loop so that explicit indexed references and directly renderable assets are handled on their own path, missing rooted files never reach the shell-thumbnail path, and ordinary shell binaries fall back to converter-based extraction only after their thumbnail path misses.

proposed_comments.title: Keep walking until a fallback can actually render

confidence.rationale: The fork validation needed extra guards for existing non-image files and non-decodable URI candidates because existence or a recognized scheme alone still let later valid fallbacks get masked.

proposed_comments.body:
### Keep walking until a fallback can actually render

**Severity:** `high`

The fallback loop should stop only when a candidate can really produce the intended icon, not merely when it is syntactically shaped like a path or URI. Local non-image files and undecodable URI candidates can still look acceptable early, but they fail only later during image materialization and prevent a later valid fallback from ever being tried.

Please make the fallback acceptance criteria reflect actual renderability, or continue with the remaining candidates when URI/file materialization fails instead of treating the first plausible-looking candidate as success.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve GenericAppIcon through deferred Installed Apps row and hero icon loading

confidence.rationale: The validated fork fixes needed both an immediate placeholder and a terminal generic fallback to keep failed deferred icon paths from leaving blank or recycled UI state.

proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve GenericAppIcon through deferred Installed Apps row and hero icon loading

**Severity:** `medium`

Installed Apps should keep `GenericAppIcon` as both the immediate placeholder and the terminal fallback for row and hero icon requests. Without that, a deferred Win32 icon request can leave a cold row blank, keep a recycled icon visible, or exhaust its candidate list without restoring a stable generic app glyph.

Please keep the generic app icon visible until the deferred request is ready to replace it, and include it as the final ordered candidate for both the row and hero request shapes.

proposed_comments.title: Thread the declared font family through protocol fallback preparation

confidence.rationale: The converged fork diff had to thread IconData.FontFamily through IIconProtocolProcessor and IconLoaderService before glyph fallbacks stopped regressing to Segoe UI.

proposed_comments.body:
### Thread the declared font family through protocol fallback preparation

**Severity:** `medium`

When an app-icon protocol candidate eventually falls back to a glyph, it should still honor the `FontFamily` that came in with the outer `IconData`. Right now the protocol preparation path drops that context, so a custom glyph fallback can silently render in Segoe UI instead of the declared font.

Please carry the outer font family through protocol preparation and use it when a glyph candidate becomes the winning fallback.
